# A multi-card drag lands in board order, and its stack shows the total

## Context

Driving #21631 (the board's multi-select example) on `dev` `4b444e4e7a` showed two places where `Neo.board.SortZone` misses that ticket's ACs. That ticket keeps engine changes out of its own PR, so this leaf blocks it ([fork and drive receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21631#issuecomment-7055099612); the stack's designer assents in [issuecomment-7055222547](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21631#issuecomment-7055222547)).

## The Problem

1. **The held card lands first.** With five Backlog cards selected in board order (Design, Build, Review, Test, Refine), a drag started on Review landed as Review, Design, Build, Test, Refine. Dragging a triage column's middle card silently reorders the selection.
2. **The proxy doesn't say how many.** A five-card drag shows the held card plus four clones and no number. The `+N` badge appears only beyond five, and counts only the overflow, so seven cards read as "+2".

## The Architectural Reality

- `getSelectedDragRecords` (`src/board/SortZone.mjs:410-465`) returns `[leadRecord, ...others]`, with the others in board order. The proxy and the drop both read that list.
- The drop moves the lead to the anchor through `moveCard`, then chains the rest with `afterId: prevKey` (`processDragEnd`, `:790-806`). The block therefore starts with the held card.
- `getDragProxyConfig` (`:340-406`) stacks the lead plus up to four clones and adds `.neo-board-stack-count` with `+${extraCount}` only when `extraCount > 0` (`:390-395`). The badge is styled at `resources/css/src/board/Card.css:176-196`.
- Design authority: `SortZone.mjs:411` reads "returns `[leadRecord, ...otherSelectedRecords]`", and `:21` reads "a `.neo-board-stack-count` badge (`+N`) for any remaining selected records". `SortZone.spec.mjs:802` pins it ("3 selected cards produce lead + 2 stack clones and no badge; 7 produce lead + 4 stack clones and "+2" badge"). This ticket amends both. The stack's look (angles, transparency, fly-in) stays as designed.

## The Fix

1. **Commit order.** The drop writes the selection in board order: the first selected card takes the drop slot, and the rest follow it through the existing `afterId` chain. The proxy keeps the held card on top. Board order is read from `owner.getColumns()` and `getColumnRecords()`, as `getSelectedDragRecords` already does for the others.
2. **Count.** For any multi-selection, `.neo-board-stack-count` shows the total (`records.length`), and the stack still draws at most five cards.
3. JSDoc for the class, `getDragProxyConfig` and `processDragEnd` names both rules. `SortZone.spec.mjs:802` changes to the total.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A drag started on any selected card lands the selection as one block at the slot, in board order. A unit arm drags the middle of three cards, and it fails on `dev`.
- [ ] The badge shows the total for two, five and seven selected cards (unit), and the stack draws at most five cards.
- [ ] One `moveCard` per record under `isNormalizing` and one `cardsMove` still hold (existing arms stay green).
- [ ] JSDoc states both rules; the board unit family and `test/playwright/e2e/board/` stay green.

## Out of Scope

The example itself (#21631). Moving a selection by keyboard. A selection across lanes. The no-op rule for a lead that already sits at its anchor.

## Avoided Traps

- **A placeholder as tall as the selection.** It breaks the sort's index math, and the one-slot placeholder plus a count says the same thing.
- **Reordering the proxy instead of the commit.** The held card stays on top, under the pointer.
